subject.title: Inconsistent message:sent / message_sent hook coverage across multiple outbound dispatch paths

question: Should outbound lifecycle hook parity be solved through one canonical core observer/plugin-SDK delivery-report seam, or through independently reviewed channel and surface-specific fixes?
rationale: The remaining gaps cross documented plugin API behavior, security/audit observers, channel streaming semantics, and Gateway/TUI result surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent contract or exception policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Canonical observer/report seam
options.body: Make one core-owned sent/sending reporting contract and require channels, Gateway/TUI/HTTP, and self-delivered plugin sends to use it or explicitly document why they cannot.

options.title: Channel-local parity fixes
options.body: Review and land narrow PRs per channel or surface, accepting higher risk of semantic drift and duplicate hook behavior.

options.title: Document limited support
options.body: Declare message lifecycle hooks best-effort by surface, which avoids broad refactor risk but leaves audit and safety plugins with weaker guarantees.

recommendation.title: Canonical observer/report seam
recommendation.body: Make one core-owned sent/sending reporting contract and require channels, Gateway/TUI/HTTP, and self-delivered plugin sends to use it or explicitly document why they cannot.

likelyOwner.reason: The source-history signal points to `steipete` across the central current files, and the decision spans core/plugin/channel boundaries.
